orthography_claude: Careful 11th-c. minuscule with many majuscule forms (Δ in δέ/δι-, tall Τ, Η, Κ, Ν/N at line end, ΓΓ in φθόγγ-). ν is usually μ-shaped (u with a left descender), sometimes V-shaped; β is u-shaped; π sometimes ϖ-shaped. Frequent ligatures: στ, ετ (ε often a curl over τ, π or μ), ει (q-shaped, with the ι rising to the upper right), ευ, αυ, θε, σθ, γεω, ων (ν as a tall stroke from ω). Iota adscript is written only in τῆι (64r.20-21, 64v.16, 65v.5, 65v.8) and ὕληι (65r.19); elsewhere it is omitted (τῆ, μιᾶ, ἐπιτόμω, ὧ, γεωμετρία, πεντεκαιδεκαχόρδω, ἀριθμητικῆ, αὐτῆ). Breathings are small dots or wedges and rough and smooth are hardly distinguishable; they are transcribed in the expected form. Accentuation is fairly full but irregular: ἄν for ἂν (64r.7, 64r.12), ὀρθώς (64v.13), ἐστιν/ἐστι/τι and χρηστος unaccented, ἅπὰν (65v.6) and μοιρὰν (65r.21) with grave; ἡ/ἠ (ἢ) written with breathing only (64v.4, 65v.2, 65v.11). Grave also before punctuation (μουσικὴ., κὴ.). Diaeresis on ι: στϊγμή, διϊστάμενο(ν). Forms kept as written: ὑπάτη διάτονος (64v.19), διεζευγμένη for -ων (64v.21-22), ἑξκαιδέκατον (65v.13). Elision is written without an apostrophe in δ'ἄν and οὐδ'ἂν, with one in ἀλλ' and μεθ'. Punctuation: the high point is frequent; the low point (often after δὲ before a definition) and a comma (dot with a tail, at baseline) also occur. Words split at line end freely (κα|λῶς, οὐ|κ, ἀ|γαγεῖν). Ekthesis of large red initials (Μ 64r.2, Φ 64v.3). No itacistic spellings noticed in these folios.

Upright minuscule with many uncial forms (Η, Κ, Δ, Ε, Γ, Τ, lunate sigma at word end; sigma forms normalised to σ/ς in the transcription). Frequent ligatures: q-shaped ει (εἰς, εἴρηται, ἔχει, κείσθω), στ (διαστήματα, διάστασις), ευ (ὁδεύονται, εὐρύθμως), εσ/εσθ (τεσσάρων, λέγεσθαι), ετ (μετά, τετράγωνον), θε, υν (looks like ω: ἀσύνθετα, δύναμιν, οὖν), ου as ȣ. ω usually in the barred (ϖ-like) form, sometimes open. ν is normally written in a μ-like form with descender and is distinguished from μ only by context; transcribed by sense. Final α (often looped, λ/δ-like at line end) and final αι are hardly distinguishable; read by grammar (ἀσύνθετα, ὁμαλότητα). β in the u-shaped form; ψ cross-shaped; ε also in a tall looped (6-like) form, used initially (ἐν, ἐκ, ἓν). Iota adscript written sporadically (τῶι 66r.12, 67r.6, 67r.7; λόγωι 66r.22; ὀγδόωι 67r.8), more often omitted (ταύτη 66r.4, τῆ 66v.2, τῶ 66v.10, 66v.22, 67r.4, 67r.6, 67r.8; ὀκταχόρδω, πρώτω, τάρτω, πέμπτω); no iota subscript. Accents and breathings regularly written; καὶ always with grave; grave often kept before punctuation (περιθεὶς., μετειληφὼς, πρός· has acute); some words without accent (μεν 66v.16, ἀναλογον 67r.11, ἡμιτονιου 67r.18, του 67r.5); oddities: διοδεὺον (66v.6), double accent in αὐτῶν (66r.22), ἄν with acute (66r.10), no coronis in ταυτὸν and κακεὶθεν. Elision marked with an apostrophe-like blob (δι' ἑνὸς, οὐδ' ἀσύνθετα, δι' ὀκτὼ, δι' ἕξ, δι' ἐννέα, εἴτ' οὖν, ἀπ' αὐτῆς, καθ' ὁμαλότητα, δ' ἀλλή-). Word spacing irregular (περι θεὶς, ἧτ τον, ἀνισο χρόνως). Punctuation: a dot whose height varies gradually from baseline to the top of the x-height (most at mid-height), and a comma-shaped low sign; the · / . distinction in this transcription is therefore approximate. Red ink only for initials in ekthesis (66r.12 Α, 67r.12 Ο, 67v.15 Τ); the red initial marks the first full line of a new paragraph even when the paragraph begins inside the preceding line (67v.14-15). The grave is kept before punctuation (μεταφορὰ·, διαφορὰ·), and δὲ often has a double grave-like stroke (״). Breathings are small round or angular dots. ν has two forms: a v-shaped one and a μ-like one with a descender (λόγων, ταχιναῖς, κατατέμνεται), so μ and ν must be told apart from context. gpt.orthography: The hand writes minuscule with large red initials and uses both full καί and its S-shaped abbreviation. Long-vowel datives frequently lack a separately visible iota; explicit adscripts have been retained where distinguishable, for example τῆι in 64r.20–21, τῶι in 67r.6–7 and ὀγδόωι in 67r.8. The unmarked dative spellings are not silently converted to editorial subscripts. The diagnosis of faint ligature-adjacent iota remains provisional in a few places. The scribe writes μελωδία without a separately visible iota, ἑκκαι- rather than ἑξκαι- in the numerical compounds, and ἔνατος with one ν. πενταπλασίων at 68r.2–3, γενομέ(νης) at 68r.13, and παιών at 69v.20 have been retained rather than normalized. Acute/grave/circumflex and point height have been followed as far as the pixels permit; some small accents and abbreviation endings remain less secure than the consonantal text. Ordinary ligatures are resolved into letters; true suspensions/contractions are expanded in parentheses.
limitations: This is a complete provisional diplomatic reading, not a claim that every accent, ligature or correction is certain. The line-specific doubts and ambiguous abbreviations must remain visible in the final deliverable.
No external transcription, web source, dictionary or parallel was consulted. Bas was consulted only after all 13 H pages had an independent complete draft.
Interlinear changes whose erased/base reading cannot be recovered are not supplied from another witness.

Decided by the editor's assistant at the editor's request.

Decided by both checkers. An iota adscript is written after the α, as in ταῖς in the same line (noted by one checker, confirmed on a close-up), hence «διαφορᾶι·»; both transcriptions lack it.
